title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: Never argue with Stage 4 price action when both the weekly trend and the four-hour momentum structure point down.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Tape Discipline

web_blocks.html: Fundamental doubts now show up directly on the chart. At the November 20, 2026 close of $341.50 (Finviz and market-facts ledger; TradingView close: $341.77), both quantitative systems classify GD identically in Stan Weinstein Stage 4 (facts stage: 4, snapshots: STAGE_4, gate: CAP_REJECTED, posture: AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN) [14][15]. There is zero stage classification split between ledgers, though we note the minor $0.27 (0.08%) session close difference between Finviz ($341.50) and TradingView ($341.77) plus TheWrap's lagging 'Base Building Breakout' tag against weak 23% (>200D EMA) and 30% (>50D EMA) industry breadth [13][14][15]. Shares have dropped -14.62% from their $400.00 52-week high, falling -6.04% over the past week and -11.01% over three months [13][14].

With the S&P 500 in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend and NO_OPTIONS_EDGE, both equity and options capital must stand aside.

web_blocks.html: Look closely at the mechanics of this sell-off. Unlike the sleepy 0.26x-volume drift seen earlier in November, Friday's -1.68% decline to $341.50 occurred on 1.26 million shares (1.01x 20-day and 1.00x 30-day average volume) [13][14]. Short interest stays negligible at 0.86% of float with 88.05% institutional ownership, meaning long-only funds—and insiders (-9.03% six-month change)—are trimming exposure rather than shorts piling in [13][31][32]. Meanwhile, the broader tape deteriorated sharply: S&P 500 breadth fell to 38.8% above the 50-day moving average across 10 distribution days, with only 3 of 11 sectors above their 50-DMA.

Notice also why the scanner's mechanical support band [$329.18, $339.20] is not a buy signal today. First, CAP_REJECTED explicitly bars IMMEDIATE_BUY and ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP in Stage 4. Second, the snapshot's mechanical invalidation stop ($330.18) sits inside the $329.18–$339.20 support band rather than cleanly below it, reflecting tight compression between the 20-day swing low ($340.69) and Pivot S1 ($334.19). Third, on the 4-hour chart, price ($341.77) sits $12.86 below its 4H 20-EMA ($354.63) with intraday_4h_turn: false and 4H RSI at 26.55—oversold, not reversing. Finally, the Options Desk scan flagged NO_OPTIONS_EDGE because no clean call-spread strikes exist above $290 for February 19, 2027 expiration, leaving zero defined-risk convex trade.

Tape Reversal Trigger: Exiting Stage 4 requires holding above Pivot S1 ($334.19) to carve a multi-week Stage 1 base, turning 4H momentum positive above the 4H 20-EMA ($354.63), and reclaiming both the 50-day SMA ($348.68) and 30-week SMA ($358.35) on >=1.2x volume as S&P 500 breadth recovers above 50%.

book_paragraphs: Chapter 7 showed that General Dynamics lacks a valuation margin of safety at $341.50 once we adjust for federal subpoenas, unfunded backlog, and unbilled receivables. Chapter 8 checks the price tape, and the message from the chart is even clearer than the spreadsheet.

As of November 20, 2026, General Dynamics closed at $341.50 on Finviz and $341.77 on TradingView. Both our quantitative facts ledger and our live snapshot engine classify the stock in Stan Weinstein Stage 4 markdown without ambiguity. Shares sit 1.98 percent below the 50-day moving average at $348.68, 3.71 percent below the 200-day moving average at $354.94, and 4.63 percent below the 30-week simple moving average at $358.35.

Look across all three timeframes—weekly, daily, and 4-hour—and you see unbroken downward alignment. On the weekly chart, RSI sits at 45.27 while the 10-week EMA at $353.35 slopes downward overhead. On the daily chart, 14-day RSI is 37.30 and the 20-day moving average at $360.48 sits atop a dense $349 to $361 supply shelf. On the 4-hour chart, RSI has dropped to 26.55 and price sits nearly $13 below the 4-hour 20-EMA at $354.63 with zero sign of an upward turn.

Price and volatility boundaries reinforce the same caution. Over the past 52 weeks, GD traded between $306.77 and $400.00, leaving shares 14.62 percent off the peak with a 14-day Average True Range of $8.02, or 2.35 percent of share price, and a 10.36 percent Bollinger Band width. While the low 0.33 beta makes GD look defensive on paper, a 6.04 percent weekly drop and 11.01 percent three-month decline confirm real downward momentum.

Volume tells you that long-only institutions are steadily lightening up rather than defending support. Earlier in November, brief pauses unfolded on quiet volume, but Friday's 1.68 percent drop moved 1.26 million shares—right on top of the 20-day and 30-day volume averages. Over the past 25 sessions, GD has logged seven distribution days while short interest remains tiny at 0.86 percent of float and six-month insider holdings dropped 9.03 percent following November Form 4 sales.

Zoom out to the broader market and the headwind doubles. Our macro facts ledger puts the S&P 500 in a confirmed Downtrend with 10 distribution days over the last 25 sessions. Only 38.8 percent of index stocks hold above their 50-day moving average, only 46.9 percent hold above their 200-day moving average, and just three of eleven sectors stand above their 50-day line. Meanwhile, Aerospace & Defense industry breadth sits at just 23 percent above the 200-day EMA and 30 percent above the 50-day EMA.

Notice also why the scanner's mechanical support zone of $329.18 to $339.20 is not an actionable entry today. First, Stage 4 triggers a CAP_REJECTED gate that forbids immediate buys or dip accumulation. Second, the snapshot's mechanical invalidation stop at $330.18 sits inside the support band rather than cleanly below it, reflecting tight compression between the 20-day swing low at $340.69 and Pivot S1 at $334.19.

Even the automated Options Desk sees zero edge here. Our live scan returned NO_OPTIONS_EDGE because clean call-spread strikes above $290 were unavailable on the February 19, 2027 expiration, and buying directional calls into a Stage 4 downtrend with an unconfirmed 4-hour chart simply burns time decay.

Sometimes investors wonder whether an oversold 26.55 4-hour RSI justifies fishing near Pivot S1 at $334.19. In a healthy uptrend, maybe—but not when Stage 4 coincides with SEC and DOJ subpoenas and a 0.65-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio. Wait for the stock to stop falling, carve a multi-week Stage 1 base above $334, turn 4-hour momentum higher, and reclaim $358.35 on strong volume as market breadth heals.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When both the quantitative facts ledger and the live snapshot agree on Stage 4—and 4-hour RSI sits at 26.55 without turning up inside a 10-distribution-day market—fighting the tape is a low-probability gamble. Let someone else catch the falling knife.
